summary_for_principal:
This closes half of another checklist item from a past session (the other half — some declared settings the engine doesn't yet act on — is still open and will be its own follow-up).

The system keeps a permanent, write-once record of every step a process takes, specifically so two overlapping attempts to do the same work can never corrupt each other. But if two such attempts genuinely did overlap — the same step, retried or resumed at almost the same moment — the loser used to crash outright with an unhandled internal error, instead of simply recognising someone else already finished that exact piece of work and moving on normally.

Fixed: all 9 places in the code that write these records now handle that collision the same, safe way — treat it as confirmation the work is already done, not a failure. Proven with a test that reproduces the exact race and crash before the fix, and completes cleanly after.

Full test suite: 365 passed, 1 new.

2. Three checklist items remain, plus this item's other half — continuing next unless you'd rather reprioritize.

interpretation.ask_as_given: Verify item (vi): RecordsPort.record_attempt MUST raise DuplicateAttempt on a second write to the same AttemptKey (spec §12.2), but nothing in engine/run.py catches it anywhere. Fix what is real, tests first, one PR per verified item or small batch of related ones.
interpretation.read_as: Confirm the claim by reading every record_attempt call site, then apply the narrowest fix that makes a genuine collision safe without inventing retry or reconciliation logic the spec doesn't ask for.

filled_in.gap: The spec's write-once guard (§12.2) says DuplicateAttempt MUST be raised on a second write, but does not say what a caller inside this engine should do when it receives one from its own write.
filled_in.assumed: Swallow it, on the grounds that attempt numbers are derived deterministically from replay position (never an in-memory counter), so two calls that land on the identical AttemptKey can only be two views of the same logical attempt — the write-side mirror of the read-side property §12.1 already states outright ("the second process calling next() against the same RecordsPort backend reaches the same answer").
filled_in.grounded_in: Spec §12.1's own stated replay-determinism property, applied to the one case (a genuine write race) that property implies but §12.2 doesn't spell out explicitly.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Low — a single helper function and 9 mechanical call-site substitutions; reverting undoes the same substitution in reverse.

decisions.headline: D30 — every engine/run.py call site that writes an AttemptRecord now goes through one shared _record_attempt helper that swallows DuplicateAttempt, instead of calling RecordsPort.record_attempt directly and letting the write-once guard's own exception propagate uncaught.
decisions.problem: All 9 of engine/run.py's record_attempt call sites let DuplicateAttempt propagate uncaught, so a genuine write race (two next()/report()/decide() calls replaying from the same durable position, both computing the identical next AttemptKey for a node neither has recorded yet) crashed the losing call instead of completing normally.
options_rejected: Catch DuplicateAttempt at each of the 9 call sites individually: rejected — all 9 are textually identical, so 9 copies of the same try/except is needless duplication for a fix this uniform.

Retry the whole node's dispatch on collision: rejected — nothing needs retrying; the durable row the losing call wanted to create already exists under the same key, written by the call that won the race, and every caller already has its own local record object (matching, by construction, the winner's) to keep using regardless of which write the store actually kept.
decisions.cost_to_change: Low — one shared helper, 9 mechanical call-site substitutions, no schema or durable-record shape change.

lessons.maxim: A write-once guard's own exception is part of the port's contract, not an incidental implementation detail — every caller that writes through that port needs an explicit, considered answer for what a collision means to it, not silence that lets the exception surface as an unhandled crash.
lessons.incident: record_attempt's DuplicateAttempt was specified and implemented correctly in domain/ports/records.py from the start, but engine/run.py — the port's only real caller — never had an opinion on what receiving it should mean, across 9 separate call sites, for the entire time this engine has existed.
lessons.destination: docs/spec/process-definition.md's own D30 entry documents the actual mechanism used.
lessons.proposed_check: When implementing or reviewing a caller of a port method whose contract includes a documented exception, confirm every call site has an explicit, deliberate handling decision for it, not just a happy-path call.
